runs.u: Can you recommend a project-management tool?
runs.reply:
Great—can you share a bit about your team and needs? A few quick questions help narrow it down:
- What kind of work? (software, marketing, ops, client services, construction, etc.)
- Team size and who will use it?
- Must‑have features? (sprints, Gantt/timelines, resource/workload, time tracking/billing, proofing/approvals, client portal, on‑prem/security, specific integrations, budget)

In the meantime, here’s a concise shortlist by use case:

- Easiest for most non‑engineering teams: Asana
  - Pros: Clean, fast adoption, timelines/dependencies, solid reporting.
  - Cons: Limited dev workflow depth; advanced reporting in higher tiers.

- Visual, customizable work OS: Monday.com
  - Pros: Highly configurable boards, automations, many views, decent reporting.
  - Cons: Can sprawl without governance; dev workflows are lighter than Jira/Linear.

- Simple and lightweight: Trello
  - Pros: Fast to start, Kanban simplicity, great for small teams.
  - Cons: Limited reporting/scale; needs power‑ups for more.

- All‑in‑one docs + tasks: Notion
  - Pros: Docs, databases, wikis and tasks in one; very flexible.
  - Cons: Requires templates/process to get PM maturity; weaker native sprints/workload.

- Software engineering (startups/SMBs): Linear
  - Pros: Blazing fast, opinionated, great triage/sprints/roadmaps, modern UX.
  - Cons: Less customizable for complex enterprise governance.

- Software engineering (scalable/enterprise): Jira Software
  - Pros: Extremely powerful workflows, Agile at scale, deep dev integrations.
  - Cons: Setup/admin overhead; steeper learning curve.

- Agencies/marketing with proofing/approvals: Wrike or Teamwork
  - Wrike: Strong proofing, request forms, workloads; heavier to set up.
  - Teamwork: Built‑in time tracking, budgeting, client portal—great for client work.

- Spreadsheet/Gantt/PMO/Waterfall: Smartsheet or Microsoft Project (with Project Online)
  - Smartsheet: Spreadsheet feel with Gantt/critical path, portfolio add‑ons.

- Build‑your‑own with database power: Airtable
  - Pros: Flexible schema, interfaces, automations.
  - Cons: Needs an admin/product owner to design and maintain.

- Self‑hosted/open‑source: OpenProject or Taiga
  - Pros: On‑prem/privacy control.
  - Cons: Heavier maintenance; fewer polished integrations.

Quick picks if you need an immediate answer:
- Mixed business team under 100: Asana or Monday.com.
- Small software team: Linear; if complex/compliance-heavy, Jira.
- Content/marketing with review cycles: Wrike.
- Client services with billing: Teamwork.
- Doc‑centric orgs: Notion (+ lightweight templates).
